newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Renault Belgium workers vote for closure package.
newsitem.headline: Renault Belgium workers vote for closure package.

text.p: Workers at French carmaker Renault's doomed plant at Vilvoorde in Belgium voted overwhelmingly on Tuesday to accept a redundancy deal.
"A total of 92 percent of the workers voted for the package," a union official told Reuters.
The vote by nearly 2,200 blue-collar workers followed a similar vote on Friday by their white-collar colleagues.

It draws the curtain on more than four months of industrial unrest following the French parent firm's shock decision to close the profitable Belgian plant at the end of this month and move production elsewhere.
Renault workers demonstrated in Brussels and Paris and the dispute soured Franco-Belgian relations, even drawing in Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene who lives in the town near Brussels.
He denounced the way in which the closure was announced as cruel and outdated.
The redundancy package offered by Renault will save 400 of the 3,100 jobs at the Vilvoorde plant and offers the remainder a combination of unemployment benefits and cash payments.
Under the plan the workers not among the 400 will not be sacked but classed as technically unemployed for two years while they look, with the help of an outplacement agency, for another job.
During that time Renault will complement their national unemployment benefits.

After two years Renault will pay a 10,000 Belgian franc ($270) premium per month per worker for between three and five years. On average the workers will get 900,000 francs gross in cash payments. Another 640 workers will take early retirement. ($1 = 37.48 Belgian francs)
